\paragraph{A complete row certificate changes the algorithm.}
A separate Lean~4.9.0-rc1 prototype proves
\texttt{mathd\_numbertheory\_541}, the original proposition for arbitrary
natural $m,n>1$ with $mn=2005$. It first derives $m,n\leq2005$.
For each $m=2,\ldots,2005$, a proved division lemma forces the only possible
$n$ to be $2005/m$. A Boolean row checker verifies that any in-range quotient
with zero remainder appears in the embedded payload
$[(5,401),(401,5)]$ and has sum $406$. Sixteen ordinary \texttt{decide}
proofs cover consecutive blocks of 128 rows, with a final 84-row block;
proved block-composition and row-soundness lemmas establish the final theorem.
This logically covers all 4,016,016 bounded cells through 2,004 row checks,
not 4,016,016 kernel cell evaluations. The payload has no authority to
accept an omitted or unsound row. External payload-generation cost is not
measured in this version.

The stock kernel accepts the soundness bridge, block assembly and final
theorem. Their reported axioms are only \texttt{propext} and
\texttt{Quot.sound}, with no \texttt{sorryAx} or native-evaluation axiom.
The complete process exits zero in 6.929 seconds, with 7.734 CPU seconds,
588,652,544-byte native high-water RSS and 572,776,448-byte sampled tree
peak. This clock includes imports, sequential initial construction/checking,
axiom reporting and 320 additional chunk rechecks. It is not an isolated
construction time or a matched historical-service speedup.

The later task groups copy the same 16 existing proof values under fresh
names and check each against the same immutable environment, using the
explicit \texttt{addDeclCore} heartbeat argument $1\,000\,000$.
Returned environments are discarded. The final theorem uses the original,
sequentially checked chunk declarations, so these groups measure parallel
kernel rechecking rather than parallel elaboration or environment merging.
The process requests eight workers on CPUs 8--15; the task-count groups run
in the fixed order shown in Table~\ref{tab:reflected-grid-groups}.
All five observations per group are retained. The first two eight-task
groups remain near the serial groups, while the last three are faster;
the cause is unestablished. These observations supply neither an
eightfold-scaling result nor a causal whole-candidate speedup.

\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{rll}
\toprule
Tasks & \shortstack[l]{Ordered group walls (s)\\first to last} & Median (s) \\
\midrule
1 & \shortstack[l]{.2829, .2750, .2748\\ .2763, .2767} & .2763 \\
2 & \shortstack[l]{.2730, .2760, .2741\\ .2732, .2741} & .2741 \\
4 & \shortstack[l]{.2749, .2746, .2747\\ .2737, .2744} & .2746 \\
8 & \shortstack[l]{.2744, .2747, .0847\\ .0867, .0851} & .0867 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Additional rechecks of previously constructed chunk proofs in one
fixed-order process. Each group checks all 16 chunks; the 20 disjoint group
windows sum to 4.934 seconds inside the 6.929-second lifetime. Earlier
construction and the final proof are not parallelized by these groups.
This is one proof prototype, not a production scaling curve.}
\label{tab:reflected-grid-groups}
\end{table}

The new certificate proves the original mathematical statement using a
different representation and algorithm. It is an alternative proof, not
unchanged-submitted-candidate verdict parity, a general extraction compiler
or a demonstrated batch-service benefit. Reflection, arithmetic compression
and independent proof checking alone establish no new systems contribution.
Coverage and cost for the complete candidate streams remain open.
